# Check of M0-d-07: closing check of consolidation round R1 (lane `check/M0-d-07-consolidate-close-1`, flow flow-7, stage group S, 2026-10-11)

## Who ran it, and how

Lane `check/M0-d-07-consolidate-close-1` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, in a Claude Code cloud container (Linux x64,
Node 24.12.0). `tools/machine_profile.py --id` printed `linux:Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz:4cpu:16gib`, which is
the expected id. The seat ran on 2026-10-11 from 12:18 to about 13:10.

This seat is an implementer-side independent closing checker. It is not the round's author; the author lane is
`build/M0-d-07-consolidate-1` (L-0417, C-0312). The round it closes is consolidation round R1 of
`consolidation/tools-plan.md` (J260, J263, J273): T-lint-0 first, then D-1 – D-8, L-1 – L-3, C-1, C-2, W-1, W-2, V-1, B-1,
the comment rewrite §2.1 and the test plan §3.1.

How the seat worked:

* It changed no file of the item.
* It ran no git command.
* It planned its probes and its mutant list before reading the author's notes rows and self-check lines.
* `tools/test_budget.py` printed 1 every time, so every vitest run used `--maxWorkers=1`.
* It ran one test process of its own at a time.
* **Before-images (its own).** The pre-round `tools/lint/` came from a byte copy in the session scratchpad. The seat
  checked every one of its 34 non-fixture files against the committed tree before using it: each file's git blob hash
  was computed with Python (no git command) and compared with the blob ids that the GitHub contents API lists for
  `plat/tools/lint` and `plat/tools/lint/rules` on `main`. All 34 are identical, and `fixtures/` is identical to the tree.
  The three persisted files (`vendor-audit.json`, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt`, `vendor.lock.json`) and `eslint.config.js`,
  `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` also equal `main`'s blobs. `vendor-audit.json` and `vendor.lock.json` equal the
  flow-7 snapshot's sha256 as well. `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` differs from the flow-7 snapshot because of C-0259, which
  landed after the snapshot was taken.
* **Mirrors.** Mirror `mb` is the tree with the before-image of `tools/lint/` put back. Mirror `ma` is the tree as it
  stands. Both are under `scratchpad/waves/check-M0-d-07/`, made as tar copies without `node_modules` and installed with
  `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`. Every mutant was restored afterwards: `diff -rq` of each mirror's
  `tools/lint` against the tree or the before-image is empty. The mirrors' `node_modules` were then deleted.

The checker's ledger row is **L-0420**. The new notes are N11 – N15 in `checks/M0-d-07-notes.md`.

## Verdict: PASS

All six failing lines of the previous check are fixed, each checked with this seat's own evidence below. No new
finding is a blocker.

* The pass changed no behaviour: no lint verdict, printed line, persisted byte or index export moved.
* Lawful-input refusals of the item's registered families stay at **0 → 0**. The whole-tree lint reports no problem
  before or after, and every fixture keeps its verdict.
* RELATED (step 3) is empty. The round changed no file under `packages/*/src/`, and nothing imports `plat/tools`.

## (3) New findings: none is a blocker

The seat ran 53 targeted mutants against the consolidated code in `ma`, one at a time at `--maxWorkers=1`. 45 were red.
The 8 survivors were each re-run against all 11 lint test files:

* **D4-guard** (the type-position guard removed) is equivalent: unreachable, per the parse probe above. Q6 keeps it.
* **C1-print** (`printReport`'s `:` dropped) is held by the common oracle's line-for-line lint output, which this check
  repeated. It is not held by a test (N14).
* **S-cjs, D1-typeskip, D2-noquery, D3-physical, D5-merge, C2-unused** each survive in the same form on the before
  code too, replayed in `mb` as B-S-cjs, B-D1-typeskip, B-D2-noquery, B-D3-physical, B-D5-merge and B-C2-unused, each
  `Tests 138 passed (138)`. They are coverage gaps of earlier rounds, not shifts or losses from R1: N7, N8, N9, and new
  N11, N12, N13. Each mutant direction is a false refusal or an unreachable input, so it fails safe.
* N15 is a note: `no-bare-pnpm`'s `run()` without a root now throws, as the other eight checks do; no caller does this.

These rows are in `checks/M0-d-07-notes.md` (hardening, M4). The seat found:

* no missing interface or test id;
* no stub or shortcut;
* no wrong result on an honest input;
* no path outside `plat/`;
* no clean-room breach.
